findings.title: Dynamic imports are all executed eagerly, not lazily per app
findings.body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an import() call, so merely importing packages/app-store/index.ts immediately starts loading all ~30 app modules; accessing appStore.zoomvideo does not lazily load only Zoom. This defeats the stated goal of async/lazy app loading, keeps the startup/bundle cost the PR aims to remove, and creates stored promises for apps that are never used (including possible unhandled rejections if an unused app fails to load). Values should be thunks such as `zoomvideo: () => import("./zoomvideo")` and call sites should invoke then await them.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions race with Promise.all(apiDeletes)
findings.body: The recurring-event branch still uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })`. Because getCalendar is now async, the pushes into apiDeletes happen after the synchronous forEach returns and potentially after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` near the end of the handler has already snapshot the array. Those deleteEvent calls can therefore never be awaited, may be dropped when the request/serverless function ends, and their rejections are unhandled, leaving calendar events undeleted while the booking is reported successfully cancelled.

findings.title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and bypasses try/catch
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the callback. Reschedule() can return true and the reschedule email can be sent before deletions finish, deletions can be lost on process termination, and a rejection from the now-async getCalendar/deleteMeeting is not caught by the surrounding try/catch (which only catches synchronous throws), producing an unhandled rejection instead of the logged error. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` discards the promises returned by the callback. Reschedule() can return true and the reschedule email can be sent before deletions finish, deletions can be lost on process termination, and a rejection from the now-async getCalendar/deleteMeeting is not caught by the surrounding try/catch (which only catches synchronous throws), producing an unhandled rejection instead of the logged error. findings.title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) / deleteMeeting(...) })` discards the async callback promises. The mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and webhooks and returns without guaranteeing the old calendar/video events were deleted, and any rejection from getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting becomes an unhandled rejection rather than being surfaced or logged. Replace forEach with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.
